overview: Epilepsy is a chronic noncommunicable disease of the brain that affects around 50 million people worldwide, characterized by recurrent seizures. Seizure episodes are a result of excessive electrical discharges in a group of brain cells. Epilepsy is defined as having two or more unprovoked seizures.
symptoms: Disturbances of sensation, including vision, hearing and taste
Loss of bowel or bladder function
treatment: Surgery for patients who respond poorly to drug treatments
prevention: Avoidance of tobacco and excessive alcohol use
risk_factors: Brain damage from prenatal or perinatal causes
key_facts: 50 million people worldwide are affected by epilepsy
25% of epilepsy cases are potentially preventable
80% of people with epilepsy live in low- and middle-income countries
5 million people are diagnosed with epilepsy each year globally
